utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I reply to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: If you could, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this part this line went through the middle of the territory of the Vozuca pocket. To the north it went on towards Doboj up to the border with the Republic of Croatia. This division, the zones of responsibility, was put in place by the General Staff so as to be able to plan and monitor the situation in various zones of responsibilities of the various corps. This made it easier for them and the corps to know what their zones of responsibility are and what are the areas they are in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I would like you to mark a few more places on this map, places that may familiar to the Trial Chamber. First of all, could you mark where Zavidovici is on this map. If you could wait just one moment, Mr. Jusic. If you could circle where Zavidovici is, Mr. Jusic. And just because we only have three colours, I'd ask that you do it in blue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks] Z.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And if you could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zavidovici is inside the blue circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And if you could put a 1 by that just for the benefit of the record, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, to correct the transcript. Page 57, lines 3 -- 4, 5, and 6. Perhaps this can be clarified with the witness. The witness clearly stated that -- that it would be -- it was easier for the corps to know what their zones of responsibility are and the areas that they were responsible for. I fail to understand the answer as recorded in lines 5 and 6. Perhaps that can be clarified with the witness as he referred to the responsibility of the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: As to the vertical red line on the map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to respond to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes. I'll ask him a further question to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Did the ABiH control of the territory within the black line on this map, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: So the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean inside the black dotted line? No, no. It was its task to control the rest of the territory that was not controlled by the Chetniks. The red line continues southwards and northwards representing the division of the zones of responsibility between the two corps. Of course when it moves through the Vozuca pocket they had no control there, but outside they were responsible in terms of security, intelligence, morale, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: So I see that on the right-hand side of the map there's a 2K, on the left-hand side of the map there's a 3K. What do those indicate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the right-hand side 2K means the 2nd Corps. To the left-hand side, 3K is the 3rd Corps. Starting from the red line, to the right there was the 2nd Corps. To the left it was the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. But to repeat that this is but a part of the line dividing the zones of responsibility. It moves further to the south and to the north. It is a complete line that was dividing each of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: In the absence of any further confusion expressed by the parties or the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution will move on at this point. Does that clarify matters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you clear, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That suffices, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And I do appreciate Madam Vidovic raising that as an issue to make the record more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, if we could go on to marking certain other locations. I'm going to ask you to mark some locations that we haven't discussed yet but will later, and that is only because this map once it's marked it will be captured as a singe exhibit, so if you'll bear with me. So, Mr. Jusic, if you could mark on the map where the Vozuca is that gives the Vozuca pocket its name. If you can mark that in blue and put a number 2 by it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this map I can only do it off the top of my head concerning the things that I remember. I know that Vozuca approximately is here. Perhaps I can put it in a circle and then mark it with a 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jusic. Now, you mentioned a place called Paljenik. Can you put a mark on the map where Paljenik is and put a number 3 beside that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paljenik is here. And the number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Could you please put a mark on the place Podsjelovo and put a 4 by that mark -- a circle and a 4 by that mark.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Podsjelovo is here. I can't see the exact marking but approximately here and there is a 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'm going to have you go to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the name of this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Podsjelovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Doesn't look anything like what is written on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I see that's been corrected, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, a few other locations and then we can move on. Mr. Jusic, could you please circle the place where the location of IKM Klek is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Klek was an observation point and later it became a forward command post. It was here. Should I put a 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Please, is sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. At this moment I do not understand, and probably you don't either, what the forward command post at Klek is. First of all, the Prosecutor needs to establish the basis of the existence of such a forward command post and then they can put follow-up questions, but we and you need to understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Wood, I got the impression you are testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: If I could explain myself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I don't mean to be. Again, the reason I'm asking the witness to mark all these place on the map is so that they can all be in one place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But has he testified about IKM Klek?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: He has not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the point. That's the basis of the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I understand and it would be ideal for me to show him the map, and then have him testify, and then mark certain places as the testimony comes up and then testify again and mark certain places. Unfortunately, I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He must testify not Mr. Wood testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I understand. Unfortunately I'm not able to do that because once this image is captured, he's not able to put more marks on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But then he must testify with this image here and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- and then establish the basis for putting a mark called Klek.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I will ask him some questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is Klek, Mr. Jusic? Or let me rephrase the question, what it was -- specifically, what its significance was to Operation Farz?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see the point I'm trying to make to you, Mr. Wood, is that these names of various places should not be heard for the first time during this witness's testimony through your mouth. They must be heard through his mouth. You've got to -- you've got to establish --

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you for your guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: During Operation Farz, where was the 3rd commander located, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Parts of the 3rd Corps command, most of them were at the area of Luka. Kamenica, Luka, at the -- or close to the Gostovica river.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And since we've mention that, could you please put a mark on the map where that is and put a number 6 by it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I want to ask one thing. Is that 6, is it Kamenica, is it Luka, is it Gostovica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Luka. Luka is a toponym. It is a settlement within a larger settlement of Kamenica. Gostovica is the river at that goes through the Luka settlement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the Luka settlement. Thank you. You may proceed Mr. Woods except that do indicate when it's convenient for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, you said part of the 3rd Corps command was at Luka during the execution of Operation Farz. Where was the 3rd Corps commander himself located during the execution of Operation Farz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the conduct of the Farz operation the commander of the 3rd command was situated at the Klek facility. This was the operation post of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And is that indicated by number 5 on the map, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On -- this is designated as 5 on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now I just have one further location. If I could ask you, sir. We saw earlier that the El Mujahid was subordinated to the 3rd Corps. Did that unit take part in this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: El Mujahid detachment did take part in this operation as a resubordinated unit of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, an objection. Is the Prosecutor trying to bring the El Mujahid into the story surrounding this map? Is this what the learned friend from the Prosecution is trying to do? I do not understand this line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I think maybe with my next question that will become more clear, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but you have an objection before you. You've got to deal with the objection before you can ask the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Well, the witness did say that the El Mujahid detachment did take part in this operation as a resubordinated unit of the 35th Division. He has also indicated that the 35th Division area of responsibility is on this map, and I can have him indicate that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I understand what you're saying. Madam Vidovic is objecting to the very fact that you have asked him about El Mujahid detachment. Now you're asking it was resubordinated to the 35th Division which -- yes, he did say so. But this was after you had asked him. You said, "Now, I just have one further question. If I could ask you, sir, you saw earlier that the El Mujahid was subordinated to the 3rd Corps. Did that unit take part in this operation?" I imagine the appropriate question to ask would be what units participated in this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll ask that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I suggest that you ask that question after the break, and we shall take the break, please. Court adjourned and come back at half past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Before the break, Mr. Jusic, I'd posed a question to you, what units participated in Operation Farz.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Operation Farz units within the 35th Division took part. The 7th Muslim; 375 Brigade; 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion, and 3rd Sabotage Reconnaissance Detachment. I think I've listed them all as far as my memory serves me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Just one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, you mentioned and marked the location for Paljenik on this map. I believe that's at number 3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: How did Paljenik feature in the plans for Operation Farz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As per our estimates, Paljenik was the gateway to enter the Vozuca pocket. It was well-fortified and an organised firing system that protected it from both sides and from the rear. So artillery and combat units defended it and it was very well fortified in engineering terms, at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: If you could tell the Trial Chamber, please, sir, generally speaking, what does the word "Paljenik" mean in Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paljenik in linguistic terms has an association of something burnt down, which used to burn, which was set alight. When one says paljenik or something burnt down, the association is with a bare area without any major plants. One associates it with a burnt-down woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Did this name have any relation to the physical characteristic of the mountain called Paljenik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Its slopes are very steep, maybe even more than 60 degrees in places. Further more, it's very steep, more than 60 degrees, from the direction of Zavidovici. It wasn't entirely wooded. There were meadows without any trees and without any woods. In places there were clusters of trees, smaller, shorter trees. On the summit itself stood -- was some 50 metres wide, the ridge itself, and in depth it was fortified in engineering terms, which could be seen from the side of the observation post that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: What was so important about obtaining the Paljenik objective?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was important because Paljenik was above a road through a gorge between Paljenik the Krivaja river, and the opposite bank. If we take into account that the Krivaja river flows along the south-west/north-east direction. So from the western -- I correct myself. South-east towards north-west. So from the western side the steeps were very -- the slopes were very steep, and the road passing below Paljenik was the main road connecting Zavidovici with Banovici and Tuzla further on. And this was its importance. This is the only road where you could transport your mechanisation. Other roads could be travelled on foot, but this road could be defended by infantry so that the opposite side could not move their machinery along it. Other roads were impassable for larger vehicles. This position was well-protected by the Chetniks, and it also provided security and defence for other Chetnik lines because it was a dominant summit. And there were some anti-aircraft cannons and machine-guns that could provide fire to the positions left and right of Paljenik, and this was proven by our operation. When it fell, very soon the other lines were abandoned. In other words, captured by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: What unit was assigned to achieve the Paljenik objective?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 35th Division was tasked with capturing Paljenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: What specific units within the 35th Division were tasked with achieving the Paljenik objective?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of the 35th Division relayed that task to El Mujahid detachment, and -- and the units of the manoeuvre battalions. I believe that the 3rd and the 4th were in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, if we could go back to the map really quickly. You mentioned that the El Mujahid detachment was involved in achieving the Paljenik objective. Do you know, sir, where it is the Mujahedin had their -- the El Mujahid had its camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know where they had their camp, although I never visited the camp. Neither did I visit any locations of the 35th Division's units for the purpose of effectuating this operation. I know of the location of the El Mujahedin camp because it was close to the road running between the forward command post of the corps and Zavidovici, and I passed along that road two -- on two or three occasions during the preparation of that operation, during reconnaissance, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: If you could, sir -- I see that you're reaching for a pen. If you can mark in blue where this camp was, and if you could put a -- indicate that with a number 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I presumed that the Prosecution would try to do this. Before us we have a map which explains the plan of the Farz operation, what we here marked are military facilities as prepared by the 3rd command corps and pursuant to the witness's testimony, but this -- this map does not show this camp as such and this is reworking the map. If the Prosecutor wanted to insert some facilities on this map which have nothing to do with this operation, then he should have used another clear map or unmarked map. What he's trying to do now is they are inserting facilities, camps, that did not exist as per this plan for the Operation Farz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. If you understand, just respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this is a map of the area. It shows the Vozuca pocket, which is important. The witness has said that the camp of the El Mujahid detachment was very close to the IKM Luka which he has indicated as number 6 on the map, and I believe it would be of great benefit to the Trial Chamber to know the proximity of that camp to the IKM considering the allegations in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic, and I just want to say that I don't understand --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- the nub of your objection, just --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document which we had before us, and I will show it to you in a much clearer form, it's been given to me by the OTP. Well, this document is a map and part of the planning for the Farz operation, and it has marked out the facilities that were done by the 3rd Corps at the time. But I'm deeply convinced that inserting such camps and facilities would be reworking the map. I don't want to negate the Prosecutor's right to show you where the camp was situated, but not on -- on the map of the Farz operation because the original Farz operation map did not show this camp. This would be reworking a document. I fail -- I did not want to object until and as long as the Prosecutor moved within the framework of this map, but now they are inserting a new facility which was not there and not done by the 3rd Corps at the time of the planning. If they want to highlight the position of the camp, they should bring a new, unmarked map, a geographical map, and do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a problem understanding your objection, and I'll tell you why. My problem is I don't have a copy of that map. I don't know whether the other Judges have a copy of that map. I don't know what is on that map and what is not on that map. All I'm told is I'm being shown a map here, and places -- things are being marked on the map, and I didn't see any markings before the markings that were made by the witness today, and my assumption is that witness is taking us through to show us where various things were during this Operation Farz. Now, our telling me and telling the Chamber that you have the map and the map was prepared for the operation. So you know more about this map. We don't know more -- anything about the map, and I'm not quite sure I follow your objection, because -- I see the witness here trying to the best of his knowledge trying to locate where various things were situated during the operation, not during the planning. Maybe the other Judges might help me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand where you find it murky. I did not want to confuse you. I have this map in colour. It can be seen clearer. But you can see in front of you that this goes for a Farz operation map. There's the key in the -- on the right-hand side, and the signature of commander Mahmuljin can be seen here now, but you saw it before that. This map is entitled "Plan of the attacking operation from 10th of September to 10th of October," and now this is a concrete piece of evidence. But now the Prosecutor is trying to insert elements into that exhibit that do not exist in this document, because he's inserting things which fall outside the framework of that exhibit. I'm not denying the Prosecutor the right to show on a clear map where the camp of El Mujahid was situated, but not on this map which is part of the plan of the 3rd Corps for that particular operation. I think that this goes for an irregular reworking of a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, we were told that the El Mujahid detachment did take part in the operation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I understood, the witness did confirm that they did take part within the framework of the 35th Division, but the activities of the 35th Division are not highlighted and marked on this map, and this you will realise and you can ask the witness about that in terms of tasks, et cetera. Because, Your Honours, if the map is being admitted as a document pertaining to a combat action, then it must stand as it is. It cannot be reworked. I grant that the Prosecution can use a clean map, but if they are trying to insert elements onto the map of the Operation Farz, then I very strongly object to that being done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But I -- I do not see this as an attempt to rework the map. The map stays as it is. What I actually do find useful is to see where that detachment was located, just as we have the 3rd Corps command at Luka. We have the Klek position. We have Zavidovici, and we have the mountains, Podsjelovo, and Paljenik. These are useful points of reference to keep together for the Chamber, and I don't see this as in any way interfering with the authenticity or the meaning of the original map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just add to what Judge Harhoff has just said. I can't understand how a clean map unrelated to this operation can give us the context in which the Mujahedin operated, if it did operate, in this operation if we are now going to put it on a clean map which is not the same map as the map that was used here, you know. Obviously, the Prosecution has the map which had the plan of the operation, and then the plan was implemented. Now, this witness is testifying not about the plan only. He's testifying about the plan, the implementation, and everything that went with it, and he's going to tell us where to his knowledge the various units that fought were located on the map. And of course the relevant unit that is at issue in this matter is the Mujahedin. So I don't -- in other words, I still don't understand the basis for the objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Your Honours. Let's deal with what Honourable Judge Harhoff said. I said that I did not object as far as the mentioned facilities and elements were marked clearly on the map like Paljenik and the others. This is the plan of the 3rd Corps map. Then we have a plan and map for the 35th Division where we will see the role and actions of the El Mujahedin detachment. But what I'm objecting to is that elements are being inserted in -- into a map that did not -- were not done by the 3rd Corps. We will later on see a map with El Mujahedin highlighted, but this map, this is very relevant for us because this map is allegedly approved by General Delic, and we -- it is important for us to demonstrate what was it that General Delic approved. And although I don't want this to be -- I'm not very comfortable with this being discussed in front of the witness, I'm not sure whether he should be hearing this, but this is the reason for my concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is just the problem. The problem is that you are -- you have knowledge that we don't have. Now you're telling us of another map that will be coming. We'll see that map when it comes, and there's nothing stopping the Prosecution showing us again on that map where the El Mujahedin was if it is relevant for that purpose. But I can't understand why we can't be shown on this map where the various units were that are relevant for purposes of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And we might, can I add, admit this map with the notion that the position of the El Mujahedin was not originally put on the map by General Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So the objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This would resolve the matter, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, if you could, please, with the blue pen mark where the camp of the El Mujahid detachment was located and put a number 7 next to that mark.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The base of the El Mujahid detachment was along this road from Luka to Zavidovici. I saw them because I passed along that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And if you could please put a number 7 by that, Mr. Jusic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: At this time the Prosecution offers this exhibit into evidence, Your Honour, this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Sorry. Just before we admit this document, when you marked number 7, Witness, I understood you to say the base of the El Mujahid detachment was along the road from Luka to Zavidovici, and you marked that. What do you mean by "base"? Let me explain what I mean. Are you telling us of where they were located during the operation, or are you telling us of where they used to stay when they are not in operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm telling you about the place where they resided from the moment when they were resubordinated to the 35th Division, and I think that happened in March or April 1993. So this was their base where they were billeted at. This is not the place where they engaged in combat operations. They engaged in combat operations elsewhere. This is where they stayed, where they ate, where they rested, trained. And I think that you use the proper term "camp."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see the question also related to camp. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: So again, Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders this into evidence, seeks to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 381.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, there's been some talk of the El Mujahid detachment. Could you please, if you recall, tell the Court who was the commander of that unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it was Abu Maali who commanded the El Mujahid, and -- and the proper term was El Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And do you know of any other members of that unit by name, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got to know another member. His name was Ajman, and I think that his duty was a security officer in that unit. I'm not certain. I can't be certain. I never saw a single document related to that, and I encountered them on maybe two or three occasions in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, you said a little bit about Paljenik and that that was a key to the operation. If you could tell the Court first of all again was -- well, from your testimony, we know that the Paljenik objective was achieved. Can you tell the Court how that came about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can tell you from my memory how this operation unfolded from its beginning to its end generally speaking, but I'm not sure whether your question concerns specific facilities, specific features, specific units or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes. I'll ask a clarifying question. What I would like you to explain to the Court is specifically how the Paljenik feature, that specific feature, how was that achieved during the operation of Operation Farz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will try and answer. On the 10th of September, the operation began. The time when it began was 6.00. The sign, the mark to move along the entire line was when artillery opened fire, artillery of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as they engaged in-depth targets. When I say artillery operation, I mean artillery of all calibre, including mortars of different calibres and howitzers, although there were only three howitzers. At the same time, infantry launched its attack. The feature of Paljenik, as I know, was attacked by the El Mujahedin unit, and it was also a part of their planning. I know they started on time, at 6.00. I know that because of the intensity of firing from infantry weapons at the feature, and it could be heard from a distance. The feature was taken in a very short time. It took them only about half an hour. And the sign that it was taken was the cessation of firing at that feature. My war experience tells me that when there is firing there is combat and vice versa. Later on I learnt that it was in our hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, when you say that -- earlier you said the El Mujahid detachment had been resubordinated to the 35th Division. When you say resubordinated, from which unit was it resubordinated to the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As we could see from the chart, it came from the 3rd Corps. It was directly linked to the 3rd Corps command up until the minute of resubordination, once the decision was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And do you recall, sir, when this decision for resubordination was made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was made before the operation at Paljenik. I don't know the exact date, but probably in May or in April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Of which year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1995. 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Where were you situated during the operation of Operation Farz, the execution of that operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Based on commander's decision and orders at the beginning of the operation on the 10th in the morning, early in the morning, I left for an observation post that was in the area of attack of the 7th Muslim Brigade. It was at elevation 923. From Vozuca or from the separation line it is to the west, some 500 metres from the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: So if I understand your testimony correctly, then, it would be about 500 metres left of the line parallel with Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have a map here to indicate it, but it was on a plane with a view of the forward command post at Luka, viewing it on the map. So if you pull -- draw a straight line between the two, the line would simply go to the east, towards the hills, and the lines of separation were some 5 to 600 metres from the observation post.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, on the map that -- the map for Operation Farz, we saw that there was a 3K and a 2K. You've been speaking about what the 3rd Corps was doing. Did the 2nd Corps have a role in relation to this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 2nd Corps played a similar role from the east to the Vozuca pocket as did the 3rd Corps. The 2nd or 3rd Corps, in the course of preparation and planning for the operation, established contact and they cooperated. They met on two or three occasions, and on one occasion parts of their respective commands got together, their commanders and parts of the staff, at the Klek feature. I don't know exactly what date it was, but in the second half of the month of August 1995. The 2nd Corps simultaneously with the 3rd Corps worked on their plan. We arranged what the line was that was supposed to be reached by the forces of the 2nd and the 3rd Corps respectively. The line was the Krivaja river. This is where they got together. Therefore, it was necessary for them where to meet and what the sign would be as well as to establish what the time is when the operation should begin. From that point on the 2nd Corps worked independently on their part of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And how much territory was liberated as a result of this operation or these two operations in conjunction with one another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly how many square kilometres it was, but around 30. That was the side of the Vozuca pocket and a northern part, north to the Vozuca pocket. In those three days of the 10th, 11th and 12th, that was the territory taken. Then there was an interruption in combat operations, and then the operations resumed on the 15th of September, 1995. I think in the initial stage the area was about 30 kilometres, and then in the next part until the truce, or the Dayton Accords, that is, another 30 square kilometres of territory were liberated. I don't remember exact figures, but this is so more or less. Around 30 kilometres in one stage and 30 in the other stage of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: How would you characterise the communication with the General Staff during and after the execution of Operation Farz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the Farz operation, at the place where I was, I didn't pay much heed to that type communication. Thinking about it now, I think communication was regular, as if nothing was happening. Perhaps on one or two occasions there were -- there were reports sent from the 3rd Corps to the General Staff, irregular reports. Other than that, communication was standard. Radio relay communication between the 3rd Corps and Zenica and Kakanj, Sarajevo -- or, rather, Tuzla. That was standard communication that existed before, during, and after the operation that went by radio relay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: If I could have the witness shown Exhibit 2249 -- or I'm sorry, document 2249, P02249.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention in particular, sir, to page 20 of that. If we could go to page 20. That is the one that bears the mark 01810470. And that is -- at the top there's an entry 14/15 September, 1995. Do you see that in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, can you explain to the Court what this document is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that this is a page of an entire log in which duty operations officers made notes as to what they could observe when they handed over duty to the next duty operations officer. I didn't used to read that log, but judging by what I can see, what I can see on the screen, I can tell you that the duty operations officer was Jakub. He describes the hand-over of duty between him had and the previous duty operations officer. There are some other elements, some other information stating that in the morning around 9.30 General Hadzihasanovic visited the command together with President Izetbegovic on their way to Travnik and Donji Vakuf. There are some other bullets here, but I don't know whether there's any need for me to read all of them. Perhaps you can be more specific. I have never seen this document, but undoubtedly this is a page from the log that was at the corps command as to any observations by duty operations officers. It was at the operations centre with the duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And why was it important for the information in this document to be accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question, because in essence all important information should be noted down. This was a document drafted by the operations officer, and he's merely letting the commander know what he could observe. To the corps commander, that is. He tells him about the things that happened during his shift. Whether he individually decided on the important things to report on I cannot say, but I think what we have here, events and information that even the commander must have known by that time. Usually the commander would have a look at these observations in the morning, but I presume the commander would already be familiar with such information. The log was kept since that was standard procedure for duty operations officers to write down their observations, to have -- to keep track of events which took place during his shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: The Prosecution offers this document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 382.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Jusic, I just have one final question. With regard to the map again that you saw before, the one that was entered into evidence in an unmarked state, you said that there was some text at the top left hand with the name "Rasim Delic" written there. Did Rasim Delic sign this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: The Prosecution has nothing further at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Jusic. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and I will cross-examine you today on behalf of General Rasim Delic. First I wanted to put some general questions to you that you were not asked by the Prosecutor. However, you did mention some of those things in the statement you gave to the investigators, investigators of the Prosecution. Do you remember having given a statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, you're one of the few officers of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina who in the former JNA held the rank of lieutenant colonel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there were seven or eight of us in total in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina who held the rank of lieutenant colonel and higher. There were several colonels as well, and maybe one or two generals.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, in the whole of army of Bosnia-Herzegovina there were seven or eight highly educated officers holding that rank or higher. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You performed many duties in commands and units of the former JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You completed the Command Staff Academy in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is the elite academy, is it not? The best academy there was in the territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the only such an academy in the former Yugoslavia, in Belgrade, at the centre of military schools. Once completed, that level of education would put you in the position of up to the commander of a brigade -- division - interpreter's correction - and one could be promoted to the rank of Colonel at the most.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were a member of the 3rd Corps, as I understood, the corps commander was Sakib Mahmuljin. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was chief of staff in the 3rd Corps, commander was Sakib Mahmuljin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when exactly you became a member of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I became a member of the 3rd Corps in 1993, in April, after I was at the -- at the staff duty in the operations TO staff in Visoko. Therefore, in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, my conclusion is that you knew General Mahmuljin well, General Sakib Mahmuljin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't used to know him very well before I arrived in the command of the 3rd Corps in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I had in mind. You had an occasion to meet him and to know him well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As of 1993 onwards, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that General Mahmuljin did not complete the military academy at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that. He completed the NCO or non-commissioned officer traffic school.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that -- or, rather, after that he completed the school of economics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war, in the former JNA, Mr. Mahmuljin worked in finances. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that before that he was an NCO in charge of training of motor vehicle drivers in Capljina. When he completed the school of economics, he was promoted to the rank of lieutenant and was sent back to the same unit in Capljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show the witness D387 now. For the record, it is an order from the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, dated the 4th of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at that. As far as I can understand this order, Sakib Mahmuljin, on the 4th of October, 1993, was appointed to the establishment post of the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps. Does this reflect what actually happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This document was implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As of April 1993, you were a member of the 3rd Corps. Is it correct that Sakib Mahmuljin, before this date, was not a member of the 3rd Corps command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. He was -- it says here that he was a member of the General Staff. That's what he told us. And there was no order on his appointment to the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at the corps ever see an order stating that he was a member of the command of the General Staff or anything similar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we just see the date of the 4th of October on this document? Thank you very much. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No problem. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 383.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about the commander of the 3rd Corps and his military education. Now I wanted to ask you this concerning the rest of the command of the 3rd Corps. On the document we saw as the last document shown to you by the Prosecutor, it was an excerpt -- it was the handwritten document. I saw a last name there. It said Ezher Arnautovic. He was the person who signed the document. Perhaps we could have that page displayed again. Could we please see the last document shown by the Prosecutor again. Perhaps we could have a look at the signatures. It says here: "On behalf of the commander of the General Staff, Colonel Ezer Arnautovic." I want to ask you something about his background and the background and education of the people drafting such reports. Mr. Ezer Arnautovic was assistant commander of the corps in charge of logistics. He was a civilian with zero military education. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are. [Realtime omission "Before the war, he was an entrepreneur] Before the war, he was an entrepreneur. That man, at the time when the war out, was over 70 years old, without any military experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, madam. That answer starting from "before the war" appears on the transcript as if it's a question. But it's supposed to be part of that answer that says "you are," full stop, as part of one answer. There must be that part that says before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you are correct. And there is also a part of the reply missing. The witness said, before the war or, rather, when the war broke out this man was already over 70 years old. I believe that is what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But before that there was a sentence that was "before the war." It doesn't look like we can get it back. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Ezer Arnautovic was a civilian who worked for the army without any military knowledge. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have a document here which reads: "Observations of the duty operations officer," and "sent." Would you agree with me that to a large extent the contents of such documents dependent on the level of experience and ability to note down and understand what was behind a certain piece of information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It all depended on his military expertise, experience, knowledge, and it is what decided what information was to be entered as significant.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at item 4. It says: "At 1900 hours, BH army commander General Delic rang and asked about the situation in the zone of responsibility ...". I would read it as stating the 1st Corps or the 3rd. I don't know. It could be the 3rd. It continues: "The duty operations officer informed him according to the reports received up until then." That was the thrust of my question. Do you agree were me that -- well, first of all, you don't know at all what the duty operations officer informed General Delic on, do you? You cannot know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's true. Nobody can tell because it's not written down anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Secondly, do you agree that it depended on his estimate of the importance of information what he will be intervening in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The information that he received from that officer, if sought, must have been accepted as it was given, and on the -- and it depended on the information what action or intervention will be taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you this: Do you agree that the fact that General Delic was inquiring about the situation in the zone of responsibility testifies to the fact that he, in effect, did not command that operation at that time? Otherwise, I may surmise that he would have known about the operation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that he did not command that operation because I took part in it, and I know who commanded because on the part of the 3rd Corps it was commanded by the 2nd -- 3rd Corps commander in the zone of responsibility of the command -- the commander of the 2nd Corps. General Staff did not have their representatives in 3rd Corps commands alongside with its commander. There was nobody from the General Staff and who would manage and direct this operation. I know that he did not command or direct the operations in the zone of responsibility of 3rd Corps, and I conclude that he did not do so in the area of responsibility of the 2nd corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is I think that he's inquiring by phone because there was nobody on the ground from the General Staff who would relay that information to him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for not making pauses between question and answer. My question is: Do you agree that he, until that time, or date, 14 to 15th September 1995, when he called, prior to that, he had not received any information about the status and situation in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. Otherwise, he would not be seeking them by calling the command.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not agree, because written information, daily combat report, would be prepared for the day that -- when he called, the 14th and the 15th September. Maybe that report did not arrive to its destination, and this is why he had no other channel other than calling. I know that combat reports were sent daily, regularly, because the superior officers of the 3rd Corps maybe did not have time to prepare the reports themselves, but they were engaged in the life and death combat situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you some detailed questions tomorrow about these reports, but do you agree that you sent regular daily combat reports to the command post of the Supreme Command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As per regulations, yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will revisit this question. Now can we take this document from the screen, and I will revisit the issue of the command over that action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just interrupt now that you're finished with this point. And this depends on whether everybody agrees. The words missing at that part page 84, line 20, where to my recollection "before the war he was an entrepreneur." I thought that's what the witness had said. I see Mr. Delic nods in agreement. I don't know whether anybody else remembers. He said before the war he was an entrepreneur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the French version that's exactly what was said. This is precisely what I heard, that he was an entrepreneur before the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To complete that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I recall this being uttered, but I could not connect it with the person. That was reference to Mr. Arnautovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before he said he was 70 years old. Okay. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask some brief questions and conclude with this part of my cross.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I asked you about Ezer Arnautovic. Now I'm going to ask you briefly about the other members of the command of the 3rd Corps. Faik Uzunovic [phoen], one of the assistants, was also a civilian without any military education?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but he was a politician without military education. He was a civilian. He engaged in politics, and he -- when he left the 3rd Corps, he entered politics. I believe that he ended up as a diplomat.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, while he executed this duty of assistants of the 3rd Corps commander he had no military education?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Civro Safet, an operative, he was also a civilian without any military training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had no military training, and his civilian education was secondary school diploma, and he worked as a football referee.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Similar situation as well when it came to brigade commanders and members of their staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was a mirror reflection.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For instance, the commander of the 307th Brigade, Bugojno [phoen] Faruk Aganovic, he had no military training; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't believe that he even finished secondary school. So he was a secondary school dropout. And I don't think that he even did his military service in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Asim Koricic, a long-time commander of the 7th Brigade, he also had no military training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Zero military training.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mahmut Efendija Karalic, a prominent member of that brigade no military training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fuad Smailbegovic, commander of the 303 brigade, was not trained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 314th brigade. He had no military expertise. He was not trained.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you agree that the personnel structure of the military commands, including the 3rd Corps command and brigade commands was of such nature that it could -- did not allow for a proper functioning that would be expected of a modern trained army until the end of the war in 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my opinion as well. I concur with that. More than 95 per cent of the persons who held important positions and posts were not trained or capable for those positions. And training of such people could not be done along their everyday duties because they would have to be sent for at least 6 to 12 months for training.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you about the communications. Do you agree with me that the burning issue was a lack of communication with the superior command in Sarajevo because of the siege of -- sorry, and I'm referring to that part of the command structure which was headquartered at Sarajevo, and I'm not discussing Kakanj. We're going to discuss that tomorrow. But do you agree that this was the real problem because of the siege?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I personally note that for a year while I was directly subordinated to the regional headquarters of Sarajevo, for one year during wartime, I could not establish any communication with my superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you specify the period?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally could not establish communication with my commander as long as I held the position of the commander of the Operational Group of Visoko throughout that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was replaced in March, towards the end of March in 1993. Until that time I had had no communication with my superior commander of the regional headquarters of Sarajevo which grew into the command of the 1st Corps later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Another thing. Communication was very poor with subordinated units in your case in the 3rd Corps. This obtained until the end of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Communications were through messenger or courier. We had very few units that we had a wired communication. Only with those who were headquartered at Zenica. Radio relay communication did not exist with other units. I think that radio relay communication had not been established until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, this is the last question about that. Do you agree that this had a direct effect on the quality of reporting from your subordinate unit to you and from you to your superior command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. Not only on the quality of reporting but on the overall command and control system.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I think is the proper time for me to stop and to continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. We will adjourn now and continue tomorrow at 2.00 in -- 2.15, rather, in this same court. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 18th day of September, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.44 p.m.,
